subject: Post-sale proposal: quarterly true-up smoothing and make-good timing
messages:
From: Novacorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@novacorp.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on quarterly true-ups and make-goods for NC-2027-114

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Procurement had a couple of follow-up questions on how Redwood handles commit true-ups and make-goods across quarters. Novacorp's finance team is concerned about large year-end credits blowing up our forecast. Specifically: 

- Do you do quarterly true-ups or only annual?
- If we underconsume in Q1/Q2 but catch up in Q4, is the make-good issued immediately in the quarter the shortfall is discovered or only at annual true-up?
- Can you smooth credits across quarters to avoid a single-year-end hit (our CFO prefers predictable monthly/quarterly P&L adjustments)?

Can you share a short proposal on timing and mechanics (proration, invoicing, and any limits on smoothing)? Lena and I are looped for procurement/finance review.

Best,
Procurement Team
Novacorp

Attachment: q3_usage_report.csv (stated attachment)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Novacorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@novacorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification on quarterly true-ups and make-goods for NC-2027-114

Hi Procurement / Lena,

Appreciate the clear questions. High level answers first: Redwood supports both quarterly and annual reconciliation; make-goods (credits for under-delivered committed volume) are typically calculated at the reconciliation cadence you select (quarterly or annual). We can propose a smoothing option that spreads net make-good credits across subsequent invoicing periods to reduce large single-period hits — subject to caps and auditability.

I'm attaching a short proposal (PDF) that outlines two smoothing options, proposed caps, and example cashflow treatment. Ben and I copied finance and legal to make sure the mechanics are feasible.

Next steps: if you like the approach we can mark it in the SOW as “true-up cadence: quarterly with optional smoothing” and include a sample schedule for the first 12 months.

Quick note on pricing mechanics: Hosted API is charged per-token. Commit tiers are applied to aggregate billed tokens for the period; make-goods are expressed as credits against invoice line items.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_trueup_smoothing_proposal_v1.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Novacorp - smoothing ask (finance/legal input)

Team — forwarding Novacorp's ask and Aditya's note. Summarized proposal idea in the PDF:

Option A — Quarterly true-up, immediate make-good:
- Reconcile usage at the end of each quarter.
- If customer underconsumed vs committed for that quarter, Redwood issues a credit on next invoice (1-2 billing cycles).
- Pros: straightforward audit trail, simple accounting.
- Cons: possible quarter-to-quarter volatility for customer.

Option B — Quarterly true-up, smoothing window (recommended for larger customers):
- Calculate credit at quarter end as normal but apply a smoothing algorithm that spreads the credit across the next N invoices (N configurable, default 4 quarters).
- Caps: smoothing cannot reduce the customer's cumulative credit beyond the calculated shortfall; smoothing cannot be applied retroactively beyond the current annual term.
- Operational note: smoothing entries are created as invoice-level adjustments with references to the originating true-up (keeps auditability).

Questions for finance/legal: any regulatory or revenue-recognition red flags with creating multi-period invoice adjustments and carrying credits forward? Also confirm maximum smoothing window we can support operationally.

—Ben

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 09:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Novacorp - smoothing ask (finance/legal input)

Short answer from finance:
- We can support Option B (smoothing) but need clear bookkeeping rules. Specifically:
  * Record the calculated make-good as a liability at the time the shortfall is identified.
  * Create amortized credit entries across the smoothing window — these are invoice-level adjustments that reduce recognized revenue over time rather than creating a single large contra-revenue entry.
  * Cap default smoothing window at 4 quarters; exceptions require FP&A sign-off.
- Need to ensure contract language references "invoice adjustments" and the right to audit the underlying usage data.

Hannah, any comments from legal on contract language?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Novacorp Procurement <procurement@novacorp.com>, Lena Park <lena.park@novacorp.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-sale proposal: quarterly true-up smoothing and make-good timing

Lena / Novacorp team —

Thanks for the patience. Per our internal review, Redwood can offer the following firm proposal for NC-2027-114: 

1) Cadence: Quarterly true-ups (Q-end) with calculation of committed vs actual billed tokens per quarter. Annual reconciliation still available if you prefer one reconciliation per year.

2) Smoothing: Optional smoothing that amortizes make-good credits across up to 4 subsequent quarters by default. Customer may elect in the SOW to: no smoothing (immediate credit), smoothing (default 4 quarters), or extended smoothing up to 8 quarters (requires executive approval and will be documented in the SOW).

3) Caps & Controls:
- Smoothing cannot increase total credit beyond the calculated shortfall.
- Credits applied via smoothing are tracked with a unique audit id and appear on each invoice as "True-up adjustment (NC-2027-114)" with a link to the reconciliation detail.

4) Accounting treatment: Redwood will record the make-good liability at identification and amortize revenue recognition per the smoothing schedule. This preserves auditability and reduces one-off revenue impacts.

5) Operational notes:
- All smoothing schedules are recorded in our billing system and visible in the customer cost dashboard; customers can download reconciliation reports.
- We reserve the right to limit smoothing for accounts with repeated underconsumption patterns; that will be a commercial discussion.

If this sounds acceptable I can prepare SOW language and a short addendum. Aditya — happy for you to share the attached PDF and sample schedule with Novacorp.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
